article_title: Model Rocket Project for Aerospace Engineering Course: Trajectory Simulation and Propellant Analysis
citation: Campbell Jr., T.A., & Okutsu, M. (2016). Model Rocket Project for Aerospace Engineering Course: Trajectory Simulation and Propellant Analysis. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Model+Rocket+Project+for+Aerospace+Engineering+Course+Trajectory+Simulation+and+Propellant+Analysis
title: Custom L-shaped thrust-measurement apparatus with piezoelectric load cell and LabView data acquisition at 2 kHz
description: Students built an L-shaped apparatus in which "The load was applied at one end of the arm and the measurement was taken at the other end of the arm", measuring thrust by balancing the moment (F1R1 = F2R2). A piezoelectric load cell fed a signal conditioner and data acquisition board; LabView scripts saved the digital signal at "a high sampling rate of 2 kHz" as a MATLAB data file used as trajectory-simulation input.
requirements: The entire experiment had to be designed using materials and equipment already available in the lab
constraints: The piezoelectric crystal used in the load cell had an inherent problem of voltage discharge, making a recorded force appear to decay over time; students calibrated the data by measuring the decay constant and multiplying the recorded data by an exponential function
target_learners: third- and fourth-year undergraduate aerospace engineering students
target_learning_goals: designing instrumentation and data acquisition under lab constraints
configuring hardware and software to record usable data
examples: Students configured the load cell, signal conditioner, BNC terminal block, and data acquisition board, wrote LabView scripts, and obtained a time-thrust curve matching the NAR-reported peak thrust of 25 N and 3 s burn time for the Estes E9-6.
